| Supported | The **GeForce RTX 40 series** is a family of consumer [graphics processing units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphics_processing_units "Graphics processing units") (GPUs) in [Nvidia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia "Nvidia")'s [GeForce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce "GeForce") line of [graphics cards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphics_card "Graphics card"), succeeding the [GeForce RTX 30 series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_30_series "GeForce RTX 30 series"). The series was announced on September 20, 2022, at the [GPU Technology Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPU_Technology_Conference "GPU Technology Conference"), and launched on October 12, 2022, starting with its [flagship model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagship_model "Flagship model"), the RTX 4090.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_40_series#cite_note-:0-1) It was succeeded by the [GeForce RTX 50 series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_50_series "GeForce RTX 50 series"), which debuted on January 30, 2025,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_40_series#cite_note-7) after being previously announced at [CES](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CES_\(annual_technology_trade_show\) "CES \(annual technology trade show\)").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_40_series#cite_note-8) The cards are based on Nvidia's [Ada Lovelace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ada_Lovelace_\(microarchitecture\) "Ada Lovelace \(microarchitecture\)") architecture and feature [Nvidia RTX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia_RTX "Nvidia RTX")'s third-generation RT cores for [hardware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray-tracing_hardware "Ray-tracing hardware")-accelerated [real-time ray tracing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real-time_ray_tracing "Real-time ray tracing"), and fourth-generation [deep-learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_learning "Deep learning")-focused [Tensor Cores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tensor_Cores "Tensor Cores"). ## Architecture [[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=GeForce_RTX_40_series&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Architecture")] Architectural highlights of the Ada Lovelace architecture include the following:[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_40_series#cite_note-9) * [CUDA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CUDA "CUDA") Compute Capability 8.9[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_40_series#cite_note-10) * [TSMC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TSMC "TSMC") 4Nprocess (5 nm custom designed for Nvidia)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_40_series#cite_note-:0-1) – not to be confused with N4 * Fourth-generation Tensor Cores with FP8, FP16, bfloat16, TensorFloat-32 (TF32) and sparsity acceleration * Third-generation Ray Tracing Cores, along with concurrent ray tracing, shading and compute * Shader Execution Reordering – needs to be enabled by the developer[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_40_series#cite_note-11) * Dual [NVENC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NVENC "NVENC") with 8K 10-bit 120FPS [AV1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AV1 "AV1") fixed function hardware encoding[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_40_series#cite_note-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_40_series#cite_note-13) * A new generation of Optical Flow Accelerator to aid [DLSS 3.0](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_learning_super_sampling#DLSS_3.0 "Deep learning super sampling") intermediate AI-based frame generation[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_40_series#cite_note-14) * No [NVLink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NVLink "NVLink") support[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_40_series#cite_note-15)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_40_series#cite_note-16) * [DisplayPort 1.4a](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DisplayPort#1.4a "DisplayPort") and [HDMI 2.1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HDMI#Version_2.1 "HDMI") display connections * Double-precision ([FP64](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-precision_floating-point_format "Double-precision floating-point format")) performance of [Ada Lovelace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ada_Lovelace_\(microarchitecture\) "Ada Lovelace \(microarchitecture\)") silicon is 1/64 of single-precision ([FP32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-precision_floating-point_format "Single-precision floating-point format")) performance. * Eighth-generation [NVENC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia_NVENC#Eighth_generation,_Ada_Lovelace_AD10x "Nvidia NVENC") encoder and fifth-generation [NVDEC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia_NVDEC "Nvidia NVDEC") video decoder, with high-end cards using 2 encoders.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GeForce_RTX_40_series#cite_note-17)
